html:
A Taiwanese engineer and business leader who founded TSMC, the Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing Company, in 1987. He created the pure foundry model of making chips for other companies, which underpins most of the world's electronics today.

Born in Ningbo, China, he fled the civil war as a teenager, studied at Harvard, MIT and Stanford, and spent 25 years at Texas Instruments, rising to run its chip business. In 1985 the government of Taiwan invited him to lead its industrial research institute. He saw that many chip designers could not afford their own factories, which cost billions, and proposed a company that would only manufacture, never compete with its customers.

TSMC grew into the largest chipmaker by revenue, producing the most advanced chips for firms such as Apple and Nvidia. Its importance to the world economy is sometimes called Taiwan's silicon shield, because a war over the island would cut off the world's supply. Chang led it until 2018. The transistor, invented in his youth, found its mass producer in his company.
